transcript.text: microwve plate wont go round anymore, food hot on one side cold on other. still heats tho

The uneven heating is very likely because the food is not rotating through the microwave energy; it does not necessarily mean the heating system has failed, especially as it still heats. The usual causes are the glass tray not engaging with the centre drive, a dirty or damaged roller ring/coupler, or less commonly the turntable motor. With it switched off and unplugged, lift out the glass plate and roller ring. Clean the floor underneath, check the ring is not cracked or missing wheels, and check the small centre coupler is not split or worn. Refit the ring and make sure the tray grooves sit properly on the coupler; also make sure the dish is not catching the cavity sides. If it still will not turn after that, the coupler or turntable motor is the likely repair.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.

ok did that. plate sits on the middle bit but wobbles, roller ring is in and the wheels spin fine, nothing stuck under it. the little plastic piece in the middle has a crack and the hole looks rounded. i did drop the plate in the sink last week and kinda shoved it back on

The cracked, rounded centre coupler is the most likely cause. It should grip the glass tray firmly; if it is worn or split, the motor can turn underneath while the plate wobbles and stays still. Do not remove the microwave casing or attempt any internal repair. For confirmation, refit the tray and roller ring and run it for one minute with a cup of water: if the centre coupler turns but the plate does not, that suggests the coupler rather than the motor. If the coupler does not turn at all, the turntable motor or its drive would need an engineer repair.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.

ok did the water test. the little 3 pronged plastic bit wobbles and doesnt really turn, the metal shaft under it looks like it moves a bit. also theres a faint grinding/clicking from the middle when it runs

[Heading: Likely cause: turntable coupler]
Unplug it first and never remove the outer casing. Replacing that coupler is the sensible next step; it should restore tray rotation if the shaft is still moving as observed. The turntable motor is a much less likely secondary possibility if a new coupler still slips. Please send the make and full model number so the correct coupler can be identified; it is usually on a label at the back or around the inside door frame. Do not remove the microwave casing.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its a Sharp, model R272WM, found it on the label at the back

[Heading: Likely cause: turntable coupler]
The evidence points strongly to the cracked turntable coupler: its rounded centre hole will let it wobble and slip on the drive shaft, so the tray cannot be driven properly. The faint clicking/grinding is consistent with that worn coupling slipping. I cannot confirm a compatible replacement from the R272WM model reference alone, so use Sharp’s official spares service with the full rating-label details, or have an appliance engineer supply and fit the coupler. Do not remove the microwave outer casing; if a replacement coupler does not restore rotation, the turntable motor/drive then needs professional repair.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
